# Set-Aside Brief

> Small business set-aside contracts open now, searchable by deadline, set-aside type, NAICS code and state. Free, updated daily from SAM.gov data.

Guides are researched from official sources, cite them, and are reviewed regularly.

## Data pages (rebuilt daily)
- [How to Bid on Federal Contracts: 6 Steps for Small Businesses](https://setasidebrief.com/how-to-bid/): How small businesses bid on federal contracts: free SAM.gov registration, NAICS codes, size standards, set-asides and responding to notices.
- [CMMC Levels and Requirements: Level 1, 2 and 3 Compared](https://setasidebrief.com/cmmc/): CMMC Level 1, 2 and 3 compared: FCI vs CUI, 15 vs 110 requirements, self vs C3PAO vs DIBCAC assessments, SPRS affirmations and phase-in dates.
- [Federal Contracts Closing Soon (Oct 2026): Bids Due in the Next 14 Days](https://setasidebrief.com/closing-soon/): 1,387 open federal contract bids due within 14 days, soonest first (next deadline Oct 29). Free, no sign-up, updated daily from SAM.gov public data.
- [Small Business Set-Aside Contracts by Program](https://setasidebrief.com/set-aside/): Open federal contracts reserved for small businesses: total small business, 8(a), WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB, HUBZone and VA veteran-owned set-asides.
- [Federal Contracts by NAICS Sector](https://setasidebrief.com/naics/): Open federal contract opportunities grouped by NAICS industry sector: construction, manufacturing, professional services, facilities support and more.
- [Federal Contracts by State](https://setasidebrief.com/state/): Open federal contract opportunities by place of performance: every U.S. state, D.C. and territories, sorted by deadline.
- [Federal Contract Opportunities by Agency](https://setasidebrief.com/agency/): Open federal contract opportunities grouped by buying department and agency, such as Defense, Veterans Affairs, Agriculture and GSA.
- [Weekly stats: federal small-business set-aside contract opportunities](https://setasidebrief.com/stats/): As of Oct 30, 2026, our daily copy of SAM.gov Contract Opportunities (U.S. General Services Administration) lists 2,983 open opportunities. 1,294 clos
- [Free downloads: deadline calendar, CSV and embed](https://setasidebrief.com/data/): Free downloads of open federal small-business set-aside contract opportunities deadlines: subscribe to an .ics calendar, get a daily CSV, or embed the next

## About the data
- Source: [SAM.gov Contract Opportunities (U.S. General Services Administration)](https://sam.gov/)
- Licence: U.S. government work; public domain in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105)
- Last data refresh: 2026-10-30
- Updated once a day from the official public data. Unofficial; always confirm details on the official notice before applying or bidding.

## Guides
- [How to Get Government Contracts for Cleaning: 7 Steps 2026](https://setasidebrief.com/how-to-get-government-contracts-for-cleaning-7-steps-2026/): How to get government contracts for cleaning: NAICS 561720 size standard, SAM.gov set-aside filters, SCA wage rules and Missouri bids in 7 steps.
- [CAGE Code Lookup: 4 Steps to Find or Request One](https://setasidebrief.com/cage-code-lookup-4-steps-to-find-or-request-one/): CAGE code lookup made practical: search SAM.gov or DLA by name, trace codes from part numbers, and know when SAM assigns one or you request it from DLA.
- [Subcontracting Government Contracts: 6 Steps to Get Started](https://setasidebrief.com/subcontracting-government-contracts-6-steps-to-get-started/): Subcontracting government contracts in 2026: find primes with FAR 52.219-9 plans, use SBA SubNet and Small Business Search, and avoid common sub mistakes.
- [NAICS Code for Construction: 2026 Size Table and Steps](https://setasidebrief.com/naics-code-for-construction-2026-size-table-and-steps/): The NAICS code for construction depends on your trade. Compare 236, 237 and 238 codes, SBA size limits and steps to pick the code that keeps you eligible.
- [NAICS Code for Consulting: 2026 Size Table and Steps](https://setasidebrief.com/naics-code-for-consulting-2026-size-table-and-steps/): NAICS code for consulting: match 541611, 541613, 541618, 541690, 541512 or 541990 to your service, with each SBA size standard and SAM.gov steps.
- [HUBZone Map 2026: Address Check Steps and Expiry Dates](https://setasidebrief.com/hubzone-map-2026-address-check-steps-and-expiry-dates/): How to use the SBA HUBZone map in 2026: check an address, spot expired redesignated areas, read your result, and find HUBZone set-asides on SAM.gov.
- [Small Business Set Aside 51 Rule: 2026 Pass/Fail Checklist](https://setasidebrief.com/small-business-set-aside-51-rule-2026-pass-fail-checklist/): The small business set aside 51 rule is really two rules: 51% ownership/control and the 50% limit on subcontracting. See both, plus a 2026 checklist.
- [How to Bid on Government Contracts: 7 Steps, 2026 Costs](https://setasidebrief.com/how-to-bid-on-government-contracts-7-steps-2026-costs/): How to bid on government contracts in 2026: register free in SAM.gov, find set-asides, and submit a compliant bid, with state portal fees and official links.
- [WOSB Certification Requirements: 2026 Checklist and Fees](https://setasidebrief.com/wosb-certification-requirements-2026-checklist-and-fees/): WOSB certification requirements for 2026: 51% ownership and control tests, EDWOSB limits, document mistakes, and free SBA vs. third-party certifier fees.
- [RFQ vs RFP: 5 FAR Clues and What to Submit (2026)](https://setasidebrief.com/rfq-vs-rfp-5-far-clues-and-what-to-submit-2026/): RFQ vs RFP in federal contracting: the FAR clauses, thresholds and solicitation wording that show which one you're reading, and exactly what to submit.
- [SBA Size Standards by NAICS: 2026 Table, Steps & Appeals](https://setasidebrief.com/sba-size-standards-by-naics-2026-table-steps-appeals/): SBA size standards by NAICS code: current caps for 20+ codes, how to pick a code when you span industries, and how it decides set-aside eligibility.
- [SAM.gov Registration Guide: 7 Steps From UEI to Active](https://setasidebrief.com/sam-gov-registration-guide-7-steps-from-uei-to-active/): A SAM.gov registration guide for first-time small business bidders: UEI, entity validation, notarized letter rules, the free process and when to renew.
- [SDVOSB Set Aside Requirements: 2026 Eligibility Checklist](https://setasidebrief.com/sdvosb-set-aside-requirements-2026-eligibility-checklist/): SDVOSB set aside requirements for 2026: the 51% unconditional ownership test, control rules, VetCert certification, and how VA and FAR set-asides differ.
- [8(a) Certification Requirements: 2026 Pass/Fail Checklist](https://setasidebrief.com/8-a-certification-requirements-2026-pass-fail-checklist/): 8(a) certification requirements: the $850K net worth, $400K income and $6.5M asset limits, the new social disadvantage rule, and a pass/fail checklist.
- [Sources Sought Notice: 5-Step Response Template (2026)](https://setasidebrief.com/sources-sought-notice-5-step-response-template-2026/): How to respond to a sources sought notice: find it on SAM.gov, fill a 5-step response template, attach your capability statement and do the deadline math.
- [Total vs Partial Small Business Set Aside: 2026 Checklist](https://setasidebrief.com/total-vs-partial-small-business-set-aside-2026-checklist/): Total vs partial small business set aside explained: FAR rule of two, 50% subcontracting limits, HUBZone price rules, and a step-by-step bid checklist.
- [Capability Statement Example: 5 Sections Buyers Read First](https://setasidebrief.com/capability-statement-example-5-sections-buyers-read-first/): A capability statement example broken into the 5 sections contracting officers check first, with SBA and SAM.gov steps, a sample layout and common fixes.
